Robert Pattinson reportedly found out he was the new James Bond just 24 hours before the rest of the world did, with director Denis Villeneuve calling to deliver the news himself. According to The Hollywood Reporter writer Borys Kit, the "process was so secretive that Pattinson was only informed he got the role Sunday morning, by Villeneuve himself." Producer Amy Pascal reportedly called the runner-ups: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, and Nicholas Hoult. "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond," Villeneuve said in a statement via Amazon News. "He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin." Pattinson himself described it as the "honor of a lifetime." The search for a new Bond has been underway for quite some time, with it being widely speculated that Aaron Taylor-Johnson would take over before Amazon bought the franchise back in 2021. Some reports say the studio initially planned to go for a "Young Bond" and was looking at everyone from Jacob Elordi to Tom Holland. This idea was clearly scrapped, however, as Pattinson is freshly 40 years old. Villeneuve is directing the pic from a screenplay penned by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight. We still don't have any plot details, but we do know it'll likely be a while before the movie is finally set to hit theaters. Bond 26 is currently undated. titre: Robert Pattinson's Batman Movie Franchise Is Officially Finished
chapo: With Pattinson being cast as Bond, DC fans are once again being robbed of a good Batman trilogy
extrait: With Robert Pattinson confirmed to be the next James Bond, one of the biggest takeaways is that Matt Reeves’ The Batman series will likely end with The Batman: Part II. Pattinson is signed on for three films as Bond, and while that’s one less film than the four-film deal that Amazon MGM Studios was seeking for the other Bond contenders, it’s pretty hard to imagine that Pattinson will juggle the role of 007 with an ongoing commitment to DC — much less Battinson’s integration into the wider DCU, which some DC fans had hoped for. To be clear, nothing has been confirmed about the status of a third The Batman movie, but the latest news combined with the extreme delays facing The Batman Part II feel like a pretty clear indication that the Batmobile has hit a dead end and will need yet another reboot. However, the loss is even bigger than you might realize, as this will be the third time in a row that Batman fans will be robbed of a good Batman trilogy. Tim Burton’s 1989 film Batman, of course, revolutionized the character of Batman and comic book movies as a whole. Before then, the general public’s awareness of Batman was mostly associated with the campy, comedic Adam West Batman, but Burton changed that and presented a dark, heavily stylized version starring Michael Keaton. He then followed it up with Batman Returns, which many still consider to be one of the best Batman films ever. Warner Bros., however, felt it was too dark and got rid of Burton for the third film, replacing him with Joel Schumacher. Keaton followed Burton out the door, not wanting to continue as Batman without him. Batman Forever, starring Val Kilmer, was the result, and while that film has its defenders, it felt like a different franchise and a different Batman altogether. The same can be said for Batman and Robin. Then in 2005 came Batman Begins, directed by Christopher Nolan and starring Christian Bale. Taking a far more grounded approach to the character, Batman Begins turned Batman’s origin into an epic film saga, where it had only been relegated to brief flashbacks in previous films. Nolan topped himself with The Dark Knight by putting Batman in the center of a gritty crime drama with Heath Ledger’s Oscar-winning turn as the Joker. For a second time, a Batman film revolutionized comic book films. Nearly 20 years later, many still cite The Dark Knight as the greatest comic book movie ever made. titre: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond – see the first look now
Robert Pattinson Cast as James Bond in Next 007 Movie
chapo: After years of rumors and speculation, Twilight and The Batman star Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's 007 movie.
extrait: After years of rumors and speculation, Twilight and The Batman star Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's 007 movie. Official 007 social media accounts confirmed the news today. Additional details about Pattinson's Bond debut remain unclear, but the announcement post did include a first look, which you can see below. "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "I'm deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team." Villeneuve also released a statement on choosing Pattinson to play 007: "Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin." The Hollywood Reporter shared additional details about Pattinson's casting and how the news was kept under lock and key in a new report. Contenders are said to have been judged on stunts, camera presence, and dialogue while testing for the role. As the competition for Bond stayed behind closed doors, Amazon reportedly became even more secretive after actually making its decision. In fact, THR reported that, while everyone online patiently awaited updates, it wasn't until yesterday morning that Villeneuve contacted Pattinson to inform him that he had landed the part. Producer Amy Pascal reportedly called the runner-ups. Pattinson has evolved into a Hollywood name that needs no introduction, but we'll break it down anyway. He first truly made a name for himself as sparkling vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight Saga in the 2000s and early 2010s. Keeping from being held within the romance adaptation box, he eventually started showing up films like The Lighthouse and Good Time. After showing up in Christopher Nolan's Tenet 2020, he went on to appear in one of the biggest comic book movie roles in history as the lead of The Batman in 2022.
